thread:
sasha: Heads-up — platform change proposal: we're going to start honoring a new routing header from clients: `X-RW-Route-Policy` that can carry policy hints (e.g. "low-latency", "cost-opt", "private"). Need SDKs to expose this without breaking old consumers. Thoughts?
eli: +1 on the feature, but breaking surface is the concern. How would older SDKs behave if they don't send the header? Will server default be safe?
maria: Default should be fallback to current routing heuristics (no change). We need clear telemetry that flags when route-hint was present vs not for quota/attribution.
sasha: Exactly — server will ignore unknown policy values, and default to route-by-latency. But we want SDKs to opt in so customers can steer. Main risks: 1) misuse of policy keywords -> noisy rollouts 2) quota attribution/console metrics confusion 3) tests across go/py/ts libs.
ben: If SDKs just expose a simple arg like `route_policy` that maps to header string, that's non-breaking. But name collision in existing options? Also need to ensure we don't silently override internal route tags used by platform teams.
eli: Could we do a shim where SDKs send both `X-RW-Route-Policy` and `X-RW-Route-Hint` for backwards compat? Server checks the new header first, falls back to hint. That avoids needing immediate server-only changes.
maria: Telemetry: add boolean `client_route_hint_present` and `route_policy_value` sampled into request logs. Console should surface a per-model breakdown that can be filtered by presence of client hint. Otherwise ops will see traffic shifts and panic.
sasha: Good call. Also we should add a strict whitelist of policy values server-side and return a header `X-RW-Route-Applied: <policy>` so clients can verify. That helps customers debug.
ben: For SDK impl: Python/TS: add optional kwarg `route_policy=""` to request call signatures and to high-level client factory. For Go: add functional option `WithRoutePolicy("...")`. All SDKs should preserve header casing normalization.
eli: Migration plan idea: feature flag in console + server-side 10% canary that honors the header. SDKs default OFF (no header). Release SDKs with docs and opt-in example. After 2 weeks and telemetry sanity, flip opt-in to ON for newer SDK versions.
maria: Rollout checklist: telemetry flags, console filter tile, sample logs exported to BI team, alert rule for unexpected quota drift. I'll own console tile work.
sasha: Devex needs short changelog + code samples. @devex-bot can you add a docs stub PR template link? :slightly_smiling_face:
devex-bot: docs: stub PR created: https://git.redwood/docs/pull/2145 — includes Python/TS examples and a migration guide.
eli: Tests: add e2e that asserts server receives header when sdk param passed, and server returns `X-RW-Route-Applied`. Also unit tests for header precedence (new header beats old hint).
ben: One more: rate-limited customers might try to game policy to hit cheaper backends. We should ensure policy is advisory only — server must still enforce quota and routing rules based on tenant entitlements. Add server-side validation that returns `400` for unknown or disallowed values.
sasha: Agreed. Next steps: ben to open SDK PRs (py/ts/go) with opt-in arg + integration test, maria to wire console telemetry, eli to add server whitelist + canary config. Aim: initial canary next week.
maria: I'll also add a dashboard tile to show "client hint vs no-hint" over time, and a regression alert for >5% mismatch in model latency when client hints spike.
ben: I'll tag PRs with `route-policy-shim` and add migration notes. Keeping header duplication for one release: `X-RW-Route-Policy` + `X-RW-Route-Hint` as fallback.
sasha: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD I'll schedule the canary and create the infra ticket. :thumbsup:
